title: Duke never fired anyone, he made them quit
summary: Bigard says Duke made people so miserable they quit; he could not do it to Bubber Miley or Otto Hardwick, hounded Freddie Guy out, and eventually fired Sonny Greer.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I've heard it said that Duke Ellington never fired anybody. Is that true?

That's true, but he made it so miserable. If he wanted somebody to leave, he made them so miserable that if they had any kind of pride within themselves, that they would just quit, and that would satisfy his ego and it kept his record clear that he's never fired anybody.
I saw that in operation with Rufus Jones in later years when he finally got to quit. Whom did he use it on earlier?

Oh, well, he couldn't do it -- he wanted to do it on Bubber Miley so much but he couldn't because Bubber Miley was the stylist for the band at that time. And he wanted to do it on Otto Hardwick but Otto Hardwick was one of the originals of the Ellington band. So that's about all. Then he got bold and he gave Freddie Guy a bad time and so Freddie just quit, and he -- I think he actually fired
Sonny because, well, Sonny wasn't doing the job. I mean, he was -- he stayed stoned all the time and he had to eventually fire him or something because he wouldn't straighten up --
